tagline: A global leader in modern go-to-market software, data, and intelligence for sales, marketing, operations, and recruiting teams
hero_kpi_rationale: Net Revenue Retention is the hero KPI because it captures customer loyalty and expansion within existing customers, a key driver of recurring growth in the SaaS model, especially in a tight macroeconomic environment.

kpis.name: Net Revenue Retention
kpis.explanation: Measures revenue growth from existing customers over 12 months, including upsells and churn.
kpis.description: The rate increases from 87% in 2024 to 90% in 2025, indicating stronger expansion within existing customers.
kpis.signal: Strong organic growth despite macro headwinds

kpis.name: ACV $100K+ Customers
kpis.explanation: Number of customers with annual contract value above $100,000.
kpis.description: The number of large customers grows steadily: 1,820 in 2023, 1,867 in 2024, 1,921 in 2025.
kpis.signal: Successful migration toward the high end

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after deducting direct costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin remains high, supported by economies of scale and the recurring model, despite rising AI-related costs.
kpis.signal: High margin typical of SaaS software vendors

kpis.name: R&D as % Revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of revenue invested in research and development.
kpis.description: The company maintains a high R&D investment rate, consistent with software industry standards, to fuel AI and automation.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: The company reduced headcount by 6% in Q2 2025 as part of a restructuring plan to support more sustainable growth.

kpis.name: Capex
kpis.explanation: Spending on physical or digital assets to support growth.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures are primarily related to cloud and software infrastructure, with no need for fabs or heavy hardware.
kpis.signal: Moderate Capex, typical of pure-play SaaS companies

kpis.name: Total Assets

risks.title: Economic slowdown affecting demand
risks.score_rationale: The risk is listed first in the 10-K with strong language ('material adverse effect'). It describes the direct impact of macro conditions on customer IT budgets, renewals, and sales cycles. Highly weighted category in an inflationary, high-rate environment.

risks.title: Difficulty renewing or expanding subscriptions
risks.score_rationale: Presented as central, with repeated mention of impact on revenue, cash flow, and profitability. Alarming language ('cannot predict with any certainty'). Renewal and expansion are critical to the SaaS model.

risks.title: Loss of data quality or reliability
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central to the value proposition ('differentiates us from competitors') and includes a contractual quality guarantee. Mentions potential refunds and disputes. High placement in the filing.

risks.title: Rise of technological competition
risks.score_rationale: The filing identifies giants like Microsoft/LinkedIn or Salesforce as plausible threats. Notes low barriers to entry and rapid innovation. Less immediate than macro risks, but structural.

risks.title: AI-driven seat compression
risks.score_rationale: An emerging risk explicitly mentioned with direct link to AI ('AI-driven seat compression'). While forward-looking, it threatens the per-user revenue model. Language is concerned but not yet critical.

risks.title: Increased regulation on personal data
risks.score_rationale: Mentions upcoming laws in 2026 and large-scale opt-out intermediaries. Direct impact on data assets and growth. Secondary but rising in importance.

risks.title: Dependence on contributor network for data
risks.score_rationale: The contributor network is key for data updates, but participation is voluntary. Moderate risk as partially offset by ZoomInfo Lite, but vulnerable to customer choices.

ai_positioning.summary: ZoomInfo integrates AI and machine learning as core elements of its value proposition. The company explicitly references an 'AI-ready' platform with an AI/ML-powered engine, as well as specific products such as ZoomInfo Copilot and ZoomInfo GTM Studio. However, the 10-K also highlights an emerging risk of 'AI-driven seat compression' that could impact per-user revenue.
evidence: Business section: 'AI-ready insights' and 'artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) powered' engine
MD&A: mentions of 'ZoomInfo Copilot and ZoomInfo GTM Studio' and 'rising AI consumption costs'
Risks: 'AI-driven seat compression' explicitly listed as an emerging risk
